thread:
Jia: Quick RFC follow-up on private control-plane reachability. We spun up two high-level options in the doc: regional edge-proxy (shared egress per-region) vs lightweight per-customer outbound agent. Wanted to capture tradeoffs and a concrete spike plan.

Matt: summary: edge-proxy is operationally simpler, agent pattern fits strict allowlist/compliance.

Samira: Edge-proxy pros:
- fewer peering/route entries
- single patch/monitoring surface
- easier regional failover
Cons: source IP preservation is harder without per-tenant ENIs/EIPs.

Samira: Agent pros:
- preserves customer source IPs (helps allowlists & audit)
- outbound-only connections are acceptable for locked-down customers
Cons: many long-lived connections and per-tenant state on our side.

Oliver: Scaling worry: per-tenant ENIs / peering quickly hits cloud route table and peering limits at scale. Transit Gateway / route servers help but cost/complexity rises.

Devon: Reliability angle: edge-proxy lets us do warm standby and fast in-region failover. Agents rely on reconnection/backoff semantics which vary across network failure modes.

Matt: Cost note: NAT gateway + regional egress charges vs per-ENI EIP monthly + instance overhead. For heavy tenants per-ENI could be cheaper; for many small tenants NAT probably wins. Need numbers.

Samira: Security: agent makes zero-trust posture easier (outbound only). We need mTLS, cert rotation plan, and compartmentalization to reduce blast radius if an agent is compromised.

Oliver: Ops: agent becomes part of customer-facing upgrade surface. Rollout/rollback story needs to be ironed out; edge-proxy upgrades remain internal.

Jia: Proposal: hybrid default = regional edge-proxy; exceptions = dedicated egress (per-tenant ENI/EIP or peering) for high-compliance customers. We need acceptance criteria to gate exceptions.

Matt: Proposed spike objectives:
1) Egress cost comparison for 3 traffic archetypes (light/medium/heavy) between NAT/regional-edge vs per-ENI.
2) Connection-scale test: simulate 1k+ concurrent agents with churn; capture reconnect histograms and resource usage.
3) Failover RTO experiment: measure time to restore control-plane connectivity for both patterns.

Samira: I'll own (1) with billing/accounting and run traffic replay for the archetypes.

Devon: I'll own (2). Plan: k8s job in test account to spawn ~1200 agent connections for 24h, capture FD counts, CPU, mem, reconnect jitter.

Oliver: I'll gather cloud provider quotas (AWS/GCP/Azure) and prototype mitigations: route aggregation, transit gateway, route servers. Will sketch cost delta for transit gateway fallback.

Matt: Hairpin NAT gotcha for edge-proxy. Example workaround for pod hairpinning:
```
# enable hairpin for pod CIDR -> external NAT ip
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 10.0.0.0/16 -j MASQUERADE
```

Samira: Also capture compliance owners and requirements: who needs static egress IPs vs who can rely on CA allowlisting. That will drive exception requests.

infra-bot: spike-ticket #INF-3248 created: "egress-routing-spike" assigned to Samira/Devon/Oliver; due 2026-04-10.

Jia: Acceptance criteria to default to edge-proxy:
- cost delta for medium-profile tenants <= 15%
- route table/peering growth stays within provider soft limits without heavy infra add-ons
- edge-proxy failover RTO <= 5s; agent fallback <= 30s
- security signoff on mTLS + cert rotation model

Matt: Telemetry: Console should show per-tenant egress mode and NAT throughput; alert if per-tenant NAT > threshold. PM/CS visibility needed.

Devon: Spike landing checklist:
- run replay for all three profiles
- run 1200-agent churn job and collect metrics
- export flow logs and monthly $ estimate for each pattern
- produce recommendation doc + slides for eng leadership

Oliver: I'll add a short hybrid decision tree to the RFC with abort conditions (cost, quota, SLA).

Samira: I'll update the RFC with compliance mapping and owners.

Jia: Thanks. If anyone needs infra quotas for the spike ping me. Reconvene in 2 weeks with initial numbers and a recommended default.

security-ops: Acknowledge. Will review cert rotation plan and agent threat model; can join spike syncs if needed.

Matt: +1 to POC visibility in Console (egress-mode flag) so PM/CS can triage customer requests.

Devon: Starting agent churn job tomorrow; will post early logs to the ticket.

infra-bot: INF-3248 updated: Devon uploaded initial reconnect histogram.

Jia: Closing thread for now; will update RFC with spike plan and owners. Ping in-thread for blockers.
